acceptance: dashboard.css --ok-green #2ECC71 -> SSOT --green-ok #35C46A (name AND value); no visual regression on the shipped cards
dashboard.css --text-primary aligned to the SSOT value #DDDDDD (now tokenized in specs/UI/tokens.css:28)
grep confirms no drifted green/text-primary literal remains in dashboard.css; cards render unchanged
does NOT touch the STOP/critical-red tier -- that is US-484-b (keep this slice mechanical + safe)

validationCriteria.action: diff dashboard.css :root vs specs/UI/tokens.css for green + text-primary after the change
validationCriteria.outcome: no drift; dashboard uses SSOT --green-ok + --text-primary; cards render unchanged

stories.goal: As the UI SSOT, I want dashboard.css :root reconciled with specs/UI/tokens.css for the two now-blessed tokens, so there is one source of truth. Both values are decided + in the SSOT: --green-ok #35C46A (Atlas A-8) and --text-primary #DDDDDD (Atlas gated 2026-07-25, US-484/BL-024). (Split from US-484; the mechanical, non-safety half.)

grounding: specs/UI/tokens.css:9-12 -- the SSOT rule: consumers render against tokens, never literals

stories.completionNotes: AC1 (green, name AND value): renamed the forked dist token --ok-green #2ECC71 -> SSOT --green-ok #35C46A and repointed all 9 var() consumers (topbar ok glyph, tile ok, ltft-bar ok, dtc-ribbon minor, longpress ring, dtc-chip minor, dtc-clear-btn bg+border, dtc-clear-result cleared). CROSS-FILE CATCH: the token also lives in JS -- carousel.js TAKEOVER_STYLE.minor.colorVar was '--ok-green'; a CSS-only rename would have left the MINOR takeover binding a var that no longer exists (silently unstyled). Repointed it + the matching assertion in tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py:847. AC2 (text-primary): dashboard.css:16 was ALREADY #DDDDDD -- it matched the value Atlas subsequently blessed into the SSOT, so this was a verify-and-pin, not an edit; added provenance comments (SSOT file:line) on the whole neutral/amber tier. AC3 (grep clean): the name-only grep MISSES the rgba() spelling -- .dtc-trust-badge[data-kind=verified] carried rgba(46,204,113,0.18), which IS #2ECC71 at 18% alpha; converted to rgba(53,196,106,0.18) (= #35C46A). Repo grep now returns zero --ok-green / 2ECC71 / rgba(46,204,113) hits outside the guard test's own assertions. AC4 (scope fence): STOP tier untouched -- a test asserts #dtc-ribbon[data-level=stop] + .dtc-chip[data-level=stop] are STILL on brand --red-light and that --critical-red does NOT yet appear in dashboard.css, so US-484-a cannot half-land the safety repoint that US-484-b owns as one coherent change. NEW GUARD (the durable half): tests/ui/test_dashboard_token_ssot.py -- 11 tests that PARSE both files and compare declarations, so drift in EITHER file re-reds (an assertion on dashboard.css alone would not catch a future SSOT edit). Also pins text-secondary/tertiary/amber-warn (already aligned) so the neutral ramp cannot quietly re-fork. GREEN in-loop: 11 new tests pass; tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 119 passed; ruff clean on both touched py files. GATES for PM/integration: black + mypy are NOT installed on the Windows dev host (same standing gap as prior sprints). VISUAL no-regression on the real panel is a PI-RUNTIME/DEPLOY gate -- the green shifts #2ECC71 -> #35C46A (slightly deeper/less mint), which is the intended SSOT value, not a regression. FILED TD-065: residual untokenized literals in dashboard.css -- (a) two .dtc-chip #2a2f37 that already duplicate SSOT --neutral-chip-bg (mechanical, no gate needed) and (b) --bg/--surface + takeover gradient edges that have NO SSOT counterpart and need an Atlas Rule-10 call on whether the SSOT tokenizes derived/darkened shades at all. Did NOT invent tokens for (b) -- that is the exact drift this story removes. NOTE for US-484-b: --critical-red #D32F2F IS now in the SSOT (tokens.css:69, Atlas gate 2026-07-26, commit 2a64549) -- BL-024 is resolved on both values and US-484-b is unblocked.

stories.title: DTC STOP-tier SAFETY treatment -- repoint off brand-red + Spool §6d multi-channel (color+area+motion+text+bg+brightness)
acceptance: PREREQ: --critical-red #D32F2F added to specs/UI/tokens.css (Spool assigned the value 2026-07-25; Atlas owes the one-line token gate -- routed). Repoint against the token, not a hardcoded hex.
repoint the DTC STOP tier + takeover OFF brand --red-light #F61D2D onto --critical-red #D32F2F (dashboard.css #dtc-ribbon[data-level=stop], .dtc-chip[stop], .dtc-hero[stop], #confirm-ok)

Spool §6d ch.1 -- AREA+MOTION+TEXT carry STOP: STOP takeover is full-bleed/large-area + pulsing motion + explicit 'PULL OVER' text; the brand mark stays small + static. (color is the 3rd reinforcement, not the 1st)
Spool §6d ch.2 -- STOP red renders on NEAR-BLACK (#000/#0a0a0a) with WHITE copy, never on brand chrome; text contrast >= WCAG-AA large-text
Spool §6d ch.3 -- deeper-and-darker axis only; NO warmer/orange shift (would collide with amber WATCH #FFC400 and invert severity order). WATCH stays #FFC400, MINOR stays #35C46A -- unchanged
Spool §6d ch.4 -- a STOP alarm is FULL BRIGHTNESS ALWAYS, independent of the US-483-b auto-dim (only ambient content dims; ties to the alarmFloorLevel guard -- STOP overrides even the floor to full)
grep confirms the STOP tier no longer references brand --red-light; UI/pi tests green incl. a test that STOP renders full-bleed + full-brightness on near-black

conditionalOutcomes: if --critical-red is not yet in tokens.css at build time, STOP + ping PM/Atlas for the one-line gate (value is decided #D32F2F; do NOT hardcode the hex or pick your own)
the pulsing-motion treatment must respect the 'motion never implies a state that isn't real' rule (carousel spec §4) -- pulse ONLY on a live STOP, never decoratively
stories.goal: As engine-safety signal integrity, I want the DTC STOP/'PULL OVER' tier + takeover to stop rendering in BRAND red --red-light #F61D2D (the brand-vs-alarm collision) and instead carry the STOP signal by Spool's full multi-channel treatment. Per Spool 2026-07-25 (offices/tuner/dtc-display-clear-safety-advisory.md §6d): the hex alone is INSUFFICIENT -- #D32F2F vs brand red differ mainly in saturation (weakest discriminator, worse on the narrow-gamut OSOYOO panel). Area+motion+text carry STOP; color is the third reinforcement. (Split from US-484; the safety half.)

grounding: specs/UI/tokens.css:69 -- --critical-red #D32F2F (Spool value + §6d semantics 2026-07-25; Atlas Rule-10 gate 2026-07-26, commit 2a64549)
specs/UI/tokens.css:50-57 -- brand reds RESERVED, brand mark ONLY (Spool S-2)
offices/tuner/dtc-display-clear-safety-advisory.md §6d ch.1-4 -- area+motion+text carry STOP; near-black + white copy; deeper-darker axis only; full brightness always

stories.completionNotes: PREREQ MET: --critical-red #D32F2F was already gated into tokens.css:69 (Atlas 2026-07-26, commit 2a64549) -- BL-024 fully resolved, nothing hardcoded; the dist declares the token once and every STOP surface goes through var(--critical-red). AC2 REPOINT: #dtc-ribbon[stop], .dtc-chip[stop], .dtc-hero[stop] border, #confirm-ok, and the takeover all off the brand reds; also carousel.js TAKEOVER_STYLE.stop.colorVar '--red' -> '--critical-red' (the token name lives in JS as DATA -- same cross-file trap US-484-a hit with --ok-green; a CSS-only repoint would have left the STOP tier bound to brand red) + the matching assertion in tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py. AC3 ch.1 (the load-bearing half -- colour is the THIRD channel): the STOP takeover keeps the base full-bleed inset:0 (AREA), gains an 8px --critical-red alarm frame that pulses via @keyframes stop-alarm-pulse SCOPED TO [data-severity=stop] so motion can never imply a state that isn't real (MOTION, carousel spec §4), and renders the existing 'REDUCE LOAD · PULL OVER' directive as a white-on-critical-red band at 22px vs the 15px base (TEXT + AREA). No brand mark exists on the dashboard surface at all (the 3-rhombus mark is the F-103 splash), so 'brand mark stays small+static' is satisfied structurally and is enforced as 'no var(--red*) on any STOP rule'. AC4 ch.2: background is var(--bg) = #000000 (one of the two near-black fields §6d permits -- deliberately did NOT invent a new near-black token, which is the TD-065 group-(b) gate), colour #fff; contrast computed IN THE TEST from the parsed tokens: white/critical-red 5.0:1 and critical-red/black 4.0:1, both over the WCAG-AA large-text 3.0 floor. AC5 ch.3: asserted as luminance(critical) < luminance(both brand reds) AND max-channel lower (deeper+darker), plus 'no warm bias' expressed as G == B (an orange shift lifts green above blue) and a >=40deg hue separation from amber WATCH; the pulse darkens toward the near-black field, never toward a warmer hue. WATCH #FFC400 / MINOR #35C46A untouched and pinned. AC6 ch.4: carousel.js brightnessLevel now SHORT-CIRCUITS `if (alarmActive) return STOP_ALARM_LEVEL` (1.0, a named constant) BEFORE any ambient math -- a live STOP overrides the auto-dim curve, the honest 0.70 fallback AND the 0.40 alarmFloorLevel; a dead/stale light sensor cannot dim the alarm. brightnessAlarmActive stays STOP-only, so non-STOP ambient dimming is unchanged (a test pins that US-483-b still works). SUPERSEDED-KEY DRIFT -> TD-066: alarmFloorLevel is now unreachable (its only consumer condition returns full). Left resolvable so a deployed config.json still parses; removal-vs-repurpose (does WATCH want a floor?) is a Spool call, not mine. TESTS: new tests/ui/test_dashboard_stop_tier_safety.py = 29 tests that PARSE both CSS files and COMPUTE luminance/contrast/hue from the token values, so drift in tokens.css OR the dist re-reds them (a hardcoded expected-hex would not). Replaced US-484-a's deliberate scope-fence test (it asserted STOP was STILL on brand red) with the reconciled assertion, and updated the 3 US-483-b alarm-floor tests to the new ch.4 contract. GREEN in-loop: tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 148 passed; ruff clean on all 4 touched py files. GATES for PM/integration: black + mypy NOT installed on the Windows dev host (standing gap); no config change so validate_config.py not required. PI-RUNTIME/DEPLOY GATE (the story's own validationCriteria): trigger a real STOP-tier takeover on the panel and confirm it reads full-bleed near-black + pulsing + 'PULL OVER', stays FULL brightness with the cabin dark, and that STOP/WATCH/MINOR still read in severity order -- none of that is reproducible off-Pi. ALSO FILED: TD-067 -- 10 non-STOP surfaces (down glyph, degraded tiles, battery TRIGGER, LTFT down, .detail-directive, clear-result reset, the #clear-confirm pair) still paint with brand --red-light even though tokens.css reserves the brand reds for the brand mark; outside this AC's enumeration and needs a Spool severity call (+ possibly a new Rule-10 token) -- note .detail-directive and #clear-confirm-ok are the two that now read inconsistent with the repoint. Plus an issue for Atlas: tokens.css:87-94 still says the STOP repoint is the 'KNOWN-open half' -- stale now; specs/ is read-only for Ralph so it is a request, not an edit.
